acceptanceCriteria: A write: or run: line that is object syntax in a source file yields no target and no command
A real write: path and a real run: command are still judged
diagnosis: Reproduced: a source file holding an object property written 'write: (' before a multi-line arrow, or a call-shaped 'write:' line, makes core/write-confinement resolve the code token as a write target and report it unresolvable; a source line opening 'run: (' is read by core/dangerous-shell as a shell command and reported unparseable (CDX-E306). Root cause: writeLineTarget and extractShellSources take any text after a leading write: or run: marker as the target or command, only write-confine's CODE_CHARS filter rejecting some quote and operator characters. Fix: one shared code-shape test rejects a bare opener, an arrow fragment, a trailing opener or comma, and a call-shaped token, in both extractors.
